subject: Data altering bug in ddply with .drop=FALSE

messages.author: fc22cb727156ff4f
messages.subject: Data altering bug in ddply with .drop=FALSE
parts:
Hi everyone,

The argument .drop=FALSE is not explicitly document for ddply, even
though it exists in the help. I figured it would work as for cast
i.e. .drop=FALSE would return all intersections of splitting
variables, including those with no data. It does that but the labels
for the split variables are wrong which means that the result values
get associated with the wrong combinations of factors:

library("plyr")

d = read.table(textConnection(
"x y foo value
1 1 bla 0.1719290
1 2 bla 0.6772318
1 2 bla 0.8376156
2 1 bla 0.5306457
1 1 bli 0.8027552
2 1 bli 0.8003605
2 1 bli 0.5801413
2 2 bli 0.4190968"
), header=T, sep=" ")

r1 = ddply(d, ~x+y+foo, function(x) sum(x$value))

r2 = ddply(d, ~x+y+foo, function(x) sum(x$value), .drop=FALSE)

r1
r2
r2[order(r2$x, r2$y, r2$foo),]

In r2 the values are in the same order as in r1, with the zeros added.
But the columns x, y and foo are in a different order. Ordering them
as in r1 reveals that the values associated with each combination are
not the correct ones.

This is a pretty serious bug since it returns a seemingly valid
data.frame (no warnings, correct dimensions) but with faulty data in
it. I guess that will tech me not to use undocumented features (plus
I'm kind of stubborn since this already happened to me with df=TRUE in
cast which was not documented and later disappeared...). But may I
suggest to remove the argument from the documentation while it is
being fixed?

Below is a patch and I also forked plyr on github (I am not sure what
is easiest, I've not yet used git for collaboration much).

Thanks in advance.

JiHO
---
http://jo.irisson.free.fr/

messages.subject: Re: Data altering bug in ddply with .drop=FALSE
parts:
for some reason, this version breaks colwise (i think.)
this:

ddply(baseball, .(year), numcolwise(mean), na.rm=TRUE)


results in:
Error in FUN(X[[1L]], ...) : could not find function "nulldefault"

with
> traceback()
7: FUN(X[[1L]], ...)
6: lapply(dfs, function(x) nulldefault(nrow(x), 0))
5: unlist(lapply(dfs, function(x) nulldefault(nrow(x), 0)))
4: rbind.fill(res)
3: list_to_dataframe(res, attr(.data, "split_labels"))
2: ldply(.data = pieces, .fun = .fun, ..., .progress = .progress)
1: ddply(baseball, .(year), numcolwise(mean), na.rm = TRUE)

any thoughts?

cheers,
-Adam

parts:

Hadley

On Sat, May 30, 2009 at 9:19 PM, anovember <adam.n...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Hi Hadley,
> it seems that rbind is the culprit.
>
>> rbind.fill(mtcars[c("mpg", "wt")], mtcars[c("wt", "cyl")])
> Error in FUN(X[[1L]], ...) : could not find function "nulldefault"
>
> nulldefault is indeed called in:
> http://github.com/hadley/plyr/blob/d9f0f45e77964a14be9078b8f8f315e4faf6d826/R/rbind.r
>
> Cheers,
> -Adam
>
>
> On May 29, 9:17 pm, hadley wickham <h.wick...@gmail.com> wrote:
>> Well something must be going wrong, because both of those bugs have
>> been fixed. I've double checked and there is no use of nulldefault
>> anywhere in the plyr source code.
>>
>> Hadley
>>
>>
>>
>>
>>
>> On Sat, May 30, 2009 at 3:46 PM, anovember <adam.novem...@gmail.com> wrote:
>>
>> > i just reinstalled from github:
>>
>> > using:
>> > R CMD INSTALL plyr
>>
>> > with the directory from:
>> > hadley-plyr-d9f0f45e77964a14be9078b8f8f315e4faf6d826.tar
>>
>> > downgrading to the cran version fixes it. (but the .drop bug is still
>> > there. (scary bug!))
>> > thanks for your help.
>> > -Adam
>>
>> > On May 29, 8:22 pm, hadley wickham <h.wick...@gmail.com> wrote:
>> >> Which version?  I posted a fix to this a while a go.
>> >> Hadley
>>
>> >> On Sat, May 30, 2009 at 2:54 PM, anovember <adam.novem...@gmail.com> wrote:
>>
>> >> > for some reason, this version breaks colwise (i think.)
>> >> > this:
>>
>> >> > ddply(baseball, .(year), numcolwise(mean), na.rm=TRUE)
>>
>> >> > results in:
>> >> > Error in FUN(X[[1L]], ...) : could not find function "nulldefault"
>>
>> >> > with
>> >> >> traceback()
>> >> > 7: FUN(X[[1L]], ...)
>> >> > 6: lapply(dfs, function(x) nulldefault(nrow(x), 0))
>> >> > 5: unlist(lapply(dfs, function(x) nulldefault(nrow(x), 0)))
>> >> > 4: rbind.fill(res)
>> >> > 3: list_to_dataframe(res, attr(.data, "split_labels"))
>> >> > 2: ldply(.data = pieces, .fun = .fun, ..., .progress = .progress)
>> >> > 1: ddply(baseball, .(year), numcolwise(mean), na.rm = TRUE)
>>
>> >> > any thoughts?
>>
>> >> > cheers,
>> >> > -Adam
>>
>> >> > On May 28, 6:09 pm, hadley wickham <h.wick...@gmail.com> wrote:
>> >> >> I just pushed a fixed version up to github.  Let me know if you see
>> >> >> any problems with it.
>> >> >> Hadley
>>
>> >> >> On Thu, May 28, 2009 at 10:43 AM, JiHO <jo.li...@gmail.com> wrote:
>> >> >> > Hi everyone,
>>
>> >> >> > The argument .drop=FALSE is not explicitly document for ddply, even
>> >> >> > though it exists in the help. I figured it would work as for cast
>> >> >> > i.e. .drop=FALSE would return all intersections of splitting
>> >> >> > variables, including those with no data. It does that but the labels
>> >> >> > for the split variables are wrong which means that the result values
>> >> >> > get associated with the wrong combinations of factors:
>>
>> >> >> > library("plyr")
>>
>> >> >> > d = read.table(textConnection(
>> >> >> > "x y foo value
>> >> >> > 1 1 bla 0.1719290
>> >> >> > 1 2 bla 0.6772318
>> >> >> > 1 2 bla 0.8376156
>> >> >> > 2 1 bla 0.5306457
>> >> >> > 1 1 bli 0.8027552
>> >> >> > 2 1 bli 0.8003605
>> >> >> > 2 1 bli 0.5801413
>> >> >> > 2 2 bli 0.4190968"
>> >> >> > ), header=T, sep=" ")
>>
>> >> >> > r1 = ddply(d, ~x+y+foo, function(x) sum(x$value))
>>
>> >> >> > r2 = ddply(d, ~x+y+foo, function(x) sum(x$value), .drop=FALSE)
>>
>> >> >> > r1
>> >> >> > r2
>> >> >> > r2[order(r2$x, r2$y, r2$foo),]
>>
>> >> >> > In r2 the values are in the same order as in r1, with the zeros added.
>> >> >> > But the columns x, y and foo are in a different order. Ordering them
>> >> >> > as in r1 reveals that the values associated with each combination are
>> >> >> > not the correct ones.
>>
>> >> >> > This is a pretty serious bug since it returns a seemingly valid
>> >> >> > data.frame (no warnings, correct dimensions) but with faulty data in
>> >> >> > it. I guess that will tech me not to use undocumented features (plus
>> >> >> > I'm kind of stubborn since this already happened to me with df=TRUE in
>> >> >> > cast which was not documented and later disappeared...). But may I
>> >> >> > suggest to remove the argument from the documentation while it is
>> >> >> > being fixed?
>>
>> >> >> > Below is a patch and I also forked plyr on github (I am not sure what
>> >> >> > is easiest, I've not yet used git for collaboration much).
>>
>> >> >> > Thanks in advance.
>>
>> >> >> > JiHO
>> >> >> > ---
>> >> >> >http://jo.irisson.free.fr/
>>
>> >> >> --http://had.co.nz/
>>
>> >> --http://had.co.nz/
>>
>> --http://had.co.nz/
> >
>

--
